newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran attacks Turk protest over anti-Israel rally.
newsitem.headline: Iran attacks Turk protest over anti-Israel rally.

text.p: Iran has objected to a protest by Turkey over the participation of Iran's ambassador in anti-Israel protests in Turkey, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said on Tuesday.

It said Iran voiced its objection when the Turkish Foreign Ministry summoned ambassador Mohammad-Reza Baqeri on Monday to protest against his role in the protests organised by a town council run by Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamist Welfare Party.
The protests on Friday marked Jerusalem Day, declared an annual day of protest against Israel by late Iranian leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini.

IRNA said Baqeri "objected to the protest on grounds of the equal treatment principle in the international law that gave him the same liberties of the Zionist (Israeli) ambassador who...had frequently voiced remarks about Iran without having been once protested by the Turkish Foreign Ministry".

"He said that for more than seven years he had endeavoured to bring Iran and Turkey closer together in a spirit of amicable relations, but that certain elements in Turkey who hated to see healthy relations between the two neighbouring countries were simply trying to torpedo his efforts," IRNA added.
Legal officials in Ankara said Turkish prosecutors had also opened an investigation into the Jerusalem Day protests in the Ankara municipality of Sincan.

The event, broadcast on Turkish television news programmes, has upset Turkey's secularist elite. A speech by Sincan's Welfare mayor has been criticised in the media as a call for the implementation of sharia Islamic law.

The mayor and the Iranian ambassador spoke on a stage draped with banners of Fathi Shqaqi, the assassinated leader of the Palestinian Islamic Jihad group, and Imam Moussa Sadr, an influential cleric venerated by Lebanese Shi'ites. Imam Sadr disappeared while on a trip to Libya in the late 1970s.
